context:
Goal: a hung CI job never turns a good change red, and a broken change never merges.
Problem (risk): read word for word, your time-limits ruling would let a change merge when a job hangs twice and its tests never run.
Based on (read): today the one required check, all-jobs-passed (it passes only when every CI job passed), goes red when a job is cut at its time limit, so a hang blocks the merge.
Based on (ruling): your time-limits ruling, Nov 10 14:09 to 14:24 CST (restart plan R3 part 2; step time-limits-end-hangs-only): stop on silence; a stop reads "stopped, no output for N min", never red and never a merge refusal; retry once, then report to you.
Departs from: on main a job cut at its time limit turns all-jobs-passed red as a failure — it reads "hung" and is retried once; this question sets what a second hang does.
Meanwhile: the time-limits lane keeps building its first part; nothing else waits on this.

lastAnswer.note: Owner picked a in the coordinator's chat, 11:51 CST Nov 12 ("this"): retry once; a second hang turns all-jobs-passed red, labelled "hung". Home: decision time-limits-end-hangs-only, written by that lane.

options.gain: No change merges with tests that never ran; a single hang never blocks.
options.how: A hung job is retried once. If the retry also hangs, all-jobs-passed goes red with the word "hung" (not "failed"), and a report names the job.
options.label: A second hang blocks the merge, marked hung
options.lose: Two hangs in a row still block a merge, against the letter of "never a merge refusal".

options.gain: Your ruling as written: a hang never blocks.
options.how: After its retry, a still-hung job passes all-jobs-passed, and a report names the job.
options.label: A second hang passes and is reported
options.lose: A change can merge with one job's tests never run.

reply: Recorded on step time-limits-end-hangs-only; the lane writes it into its decision.
short: CI: a job that hangs twice
title: When a CI job hangs, is retried, and hangs again, should the merge still be blocked?
why: Recommended: a. It keeps the outcome your ruling protects (a hang never blocks a good change by itself) without letting a change merge untested.
